paragraphs.text: The clerics saw her as a divine gift. She saw them only as allies in her war against Phage.
Ixidor had only to imagine their ruin and Akroma made it so.
"We have faced horrors of war and terrors beyond imagining. We will overcome the uncertainties of this new life."
"The hum of the universe is never off-key." —Mystic elder
Every day, Order clerics contain as much of the Mirari's energy as possible, hoping to delay Otaria's demise.
He represents what little pride the Order has left.
"Every question has a proper answer. Every soul has a proper place."
"Death never stops to rest. Neither can we."
"There's no 'I' in 'team,' but there's a 'we' in 'weapon.'"
Together they could hit anything between the heavens and the horizon.
Enlightenment comes most swiftly at life's end.
"The rabble likes them. Make sure they win, then book them for tomorrow." —Cabal Patriarch
"Honor, guide my step."
Success is one part inspiration, nine parts desperation.
Although the Order frowned upon his preparations for the pits, behind closed doors most saw the fights as a necessary evil.
"I will wield the stone of my homeland as though it were the fists of the Ancestor."
"Only on the battlefield can we repay all the Order has given us."
"The truth will outshine all lies."
Dread was as foreign to her as the landscape ahead.
"Your graves will lie beneath my final nest."
"Share your devotion with me."
"Like any pests, goblins must be repelled quickly or they multiply."
The turning of the tide always begins with one soldier's decision to head back into the fray.
"Everyone deserves a chance to live. My job is to make sure they get it."
Banking steeply, the aven streaked toward the ground—and vanished.
Cabal spies trying to follow the Order's movements are constantly frustrated by tracks that stop dead.
"Our death-arrows flew in high arcs towards the aven. And then . . . nothing." —Coliseum guard
Entire platoons have mysteriously vanished from battle, leaving enemy weapons to slice through empty air.
They're trained in the art of pressing their luck.
"There is no greater burden than choosing who to save." —Kamahl, druid acolyte
"I trust what I make for myself. Do you trust more what is made for you by another?"
"We will force the Cabal into their own pits!"
Light's champion in the stronghold of darkness.
Newcomers to Otaria find themselves at the bottom of the heap. In the pits, they at least have the chance to climb atop a heap of bodies.
"Our noblest thoughts are our very first and our very last."
"A richer people could give more but they could never give as much."
Even those born to battle could only lay their blades at Akroma's feet.
"Until the world unites in vengeful fury and Phage is destroyed, I will not stay my hand." —Akroma, angelic avenger
"Those who live by the sword will die by the sword. I choose to do neither."
"Win together, die alone."
"You may fight if I deem your cause worthy."
"We lay our dead to rest in a beautiful bed, in hopes that the Ancestor will think it a fit cradle for the next life." —Mystic elder
So great is his certainty that mere facts cannot shake it.
The tall, reedy grass of the Daru Plains rustles loudly in the winds, a perfect cover for any ambush.
His bolas whirl like galaxies, but it's his enemies who see stars.
"The faithful don't succumb to terror, nor are they ruled by passion. They adhere to order, for order is life." —*Volume I, The Book of Faith*
"We help our Southern Order comrades as much as we can. But the Cabal's insidious influence spreads, dividing our forces and leaving new arrivals to fend for themselves." —Commander Eesha
Most refugees left their ancestral homes behind when they came to Otaria. A few decided to bring them along.
He brews trouble.
Aphetto con artists started working in pairs to make it less likely they'd be the victims of con artists.
He has journeyed where none have been before. Now he returns to ensure that none follow.
Some things are better left unknown.
"I'll leave subtlety to the rich."
The most valuable commodity in the pits is a way out.
"Wisdom, clear my eyes."
"I said 'pick his brain,' not 'tear off his head.'" —Riptide Project researcher
"Like the seas, the Æther is fickle and ever-changing. If we can control one, we can master the other." —Riptide Project director
"Show weakness to hide your strength."
"Shaping reality is simply a matter of knowing where to apply pressure." —Ixidor, reality sculptor
"Don't become so enthralled with magic that you forget you can fly without it."
"My past holds only pain and loss. I will conquer it by creating the perfect future." —Ixidor, reality sculptor
"Attempts to revive this ancient species have not been entirely successful, but results indicate potential for future development." —Riptide Project researcher
When Otarians learned not to trust wizards, the wizards learned to adapt.
"One wizard is a suspect. Two wizards are a conspiracy." —Elvish refugee
"Reality has exiled me. I am no longer bound by its laws."
"Some dreams should not come to be."
"Next time, don't bother."
Strength may win the fight, but style wins the crowd.
Devotion, the second myth of reality: The faithful are most hurt by the objects of their faith.
Trust, the fifth myth of reality: Every truth holds the seed of betrayal.
Familiarity, the first myth of reality: What you know the best, you observe the least.
Conviction, the third myth of reality: Only those who seek the truth can be deceived.
Fellowship, the fourth myth of reality: As the tides of war shift, so do loyalties.
"Open your mind to me."
The Riptide Project was perhaps the only school devoted to preventing the spread of knowledge.
"The world is a puzzle, and the mind is its key."
"Leave the door to the past even slightly ajar and it could be blown off its hinges."
"I gave it two choices: life in the lab or death in the hunt."
The wizard consulted the Riptide Project about how to further his research. He wasn't prepared for what they told him.
"I've got everything you'd ever need right here. Just give me some time to find it."
From their mountain aeries, aven scholars see far more than the distant horizon.
"My vengeance will drown my enemies as my storms drown the desert." —Ixidor, reality sculptor
"It's a fine way to travel, if you don't mind the smell."
At that point, the wizards' argument got a lot uglier.
"It's hard to fight on an empty mind."
"Be logical in all things. Do not allow instinct or passion to cloud your mind." —*Volume II, The Book of Insight*
"The Cabal mocks the natural order. For its minions, death is just a pause between duties." —Kamahl, druid acolyte
Aphetto's swamps are alive with the dead.
Phage became both executioner and savior, helping others to the same rebirth she had found.
Even the most virtuous person is only one secret away from being owned by the Cabal.
Nothing comes together as easily as it comes apart.
"You are weak. I am strong. The protocol is obvious."
"In its natural habitat, the goblin is stupid, yet devious. Now it's stupid, devious, and powerful."
"Darkness, hide my fear."
Few Cabal fighters fear death. They fear what follows it.
The Cabal breeds many things for the pit fights, but it never breeds compassion.
The lantern he carried did not light his way—it signaled his approach.
"His sacrifice shall not be forgotten. Now toss his body over there with the others." —Phage the Untouchable
Proper burial is a luxury Otarians can no longer afford.
The most terrifying zombies are those with just a hint of their old selves left.
"I do unto others as others have done unto me." —Phage the Untouchable
It wasn't as much a strategy as a dim instinct to drown their prey.
In life, it was a fetid, disease-ridden thing. In death, not much changed.
Cabal clerics don't heal the sick—they heal the dead.
Greed and gluttony led him to death. Now they are his greatest assets.
The Cabal never expected its creations to create servants of their own.
It's drawn to the scent of screaming.
"It is from Phage that this evil springs, and to her it shall return." —Akroma, angelic avenger
The soul sheds light, and death is its shadow. When the light dims, life and death embrace. —Nantuko teaching
"Family plots are so convenient." —Cabal Patriarch
"We have ways to make you talk, but you have nothing interesting to say."
It's always hungry, yet easily sated.
No one in Aphetto answers a knock at the door after sundown.
The grim business of the Coliseum casts long shadows.
"My priests swore loyalty to the Cabal not until death, but beyond it." —Cabal Patriarch
"I can't hear them scream, but at least I don't have to listen to them beg." —Phage the Untouchable
"Surrender your soul to me."
"How cute. Does it do any other tricks?" —Braids, dementia summoner
"If you can't pay your gambling debts, you just might be tomorrow's main attraction at the Grand Coliseum."
Few who cross Phage have the chance to repeat the mistake.
When tempers run high, it's easy to lose your head.
As Phage drank their energy, a vague memory of Jeska stirred. Then she lost herself again in the joy of her victims' suffering.
It just obeys you. It doesn't *like* you.
"My eyes are my strongest feature."
Such sacrilege turns blinding grief into blinding rage.
"Terror corrupts order and paralyzes instinct." —*Volume III, The Book of Decay*
The only prince inside this frog is the one it ate.
"Is it just me, or does that meteor have teeth?"
It has two kinds of droppings, neither of which is particularly pleasant.
Their skeletons can be found all over Skirk Ridge, tangled in each other's horns.
There are two ways to resolve puzzling situations: thoughtful contemplation or force. After thoughtful contemplation, most barbarians choose force.
Wizards fought over the stone to exploit its power. Goblins fight over it because it's shiny.
It can kill you with three arms tied behind its back.
Goblins prize its hide for building rock sled runners.
"Passion, fire my heart."
Goblins resolve disputes by splitting everything straight down the middle.
A powerful mage created the roost to guard a portal between the planes. The mage is long gone, but dragons still keep watch at the gate.
"Life is too short for something like a hunk of rock to get in my way."
Throw enough goblins at any problem and it should go away. At the very least, there'll be fewer goblins.
"The good news is, we figured out how the wand works. The bad news is, we figured out how the wand works."
The goblin word for "flying" is more accurately translated as "falling slowly."
"Let's play 'sled.' Here's how it works: you're the sled."
For some reason, goblin fighting school isn't as crowded on day two.
Hot blood washes away cold reason.
Only the Cabal could make a fight to the death more deadly.
"Maybe they wanted to be on the winning side for once." —Matoc, lavamancer
Skirk Ridge had survived earthquakes, mudslides, and meteor showers. Then the goblins moved in.
Options will cost you, but a lack of them will cost you even more.
When the ground is saturated with mana, even the lightest footstep can bring it to the surface.
To his surprise, Furt discovered that the strange creatures were not at all like bugs.
"Some solve problems by thinking and talking. Others use rocks." —Toggo, goblin weaponsmith
"Release chaos with me!"
In the smoldering ashes of Shiv, a few dragons strive to rebuild their native land. The rest seek any opportunity to restore the broken pride of their race.
Zemoo found out the hard way that "inflammable" and "flammable" mean the same thing.
Its only predators are the elements.
"I love lightning! It's my best invention since the rock." —Toggo, goblin weaponsmith
He's boss because he's smart enough to get out of the way.
"I like goblins. They make funny little popping sounds when they die." —Braids, dementia summoner
"If it didn't hurt, how would I know it worked?"
"Wait 'til Toggo sees this!"
After a few painful experiences, goblins learned not to pick their noses around the beasts.
Pardic barbarians didn't complain when the Order started blaming every crisis on the Cabal.
Efforts to use them as spies failed when they kept reporting to the enemy.
Goblins' motivational techniques are crude, but effective.
"Darius?" "Yeah?" "There's a goblin sneaking up on you." "So?" "Just sayin'."
"Passions can't be shackled by laws or mastered with logic. The choice is freedom or death." —*Volume IV, The Book of Fire*
Anywhere else they would be hunted for their skins, but in Wirewood, they are safe.
"I have seen life's purpose, and now it is my own." —Kamahl, druid acolyte
Every creature of the forest has a name, and she knows them all.
The Mirari called to the centaurs, and all who heard it were forever changed.
"Life, be my shield."
"Wirewood cannot hide great size. Only with speed and skill can we survive here."
"Old home never forgotten, new home ours forever."
In harsh times, the strongest currency is cooperation.
"Destruction is the work of an afternoon. Creation is the work of a lifetime." —Kamahl, druid acolyte
"The stories tell of a distant time when machines overran the forests, destroying everything that lived. That time will not come again."
"Our lives are woven together like the trees' branches over our heads, forming a canopy that protects us all."
"My tales of war are the stories most asked for around the fires at night, but they're the ones I care least to tell."
"The wise learn from successes as well as mistakes."
Torching Krosa would be pointless. It grows faster than it burns.
"Channel your vitality through me."
The Mirari's echoes rang in the scouts' minds long after they had returned from the Krosan Forest.
"My mind has changed. My strength has not."
As Krosa unleashed the peace in Kamahl, he unleashed the fury in Krosa.
When it walked, it altered geography. When it bellowed, it changed the weather.
You know it's coming when you hear the distant thunder. You know where it's been when you see the path of broken trees.
It emerges from the mists only to feed.
The blood of Krosa turns rational beings into primal forces.
"From here, let the world be reborn."
The biggest difference between a victory and a massacre is which side you're on.
"All we know about the Krosan Forest we have learned from those few who made it out alive." —Elvish refugee
Wirewood's beasts didn't seem to mind when the elves moved in. In fact, they hardly noticed them underfoot.
The only thing that flies over the Krosan Forest is the wind.
He was born of the Mirari, thrust out of his homeland before he was even aware. Left without purpose or meaning, he found both in the pits.
Most creatures in the Krosan Forest feared the Mirari's power. A few fed upon it.
Its voice crackles with the hum of a thousand wings beating at once.
No one in Wirewood understands what is happening. They just know it's unnatural—and coming from Krosa.
The insects found a meal in the carrion of the beast's prey. The beast found a spiffy new hairstyle.
The elves arriving in Wirewood had no homes, let alone weapons, but they knew that the forest would always provide.
The insects keep the wurm's hide free from parasites. In return, the wurm doesn't eat the insects.
The safety of the village depends on the beast thinking with its stomach.
The Mirari twisted all that lived in the Krosan Forest into gross mockeries of their former selves.
No matter your strength, the Krosan Forest is stronger. No matter your speed, the Wirewood Forest is faster.
Kamahl left the violence of his former life behind him, but he still believes in the power of muscle.
The ritual of making draws upon the elves' memories and pasts. And elves have long memories and ancient pasts.
Mulch is the fabric of life in the forest. Plants live in it, they die in it, and then they become part of it, feeding countless generations to come.
Krosa's distorted groves bear strange fruit.
"Close your ears to the voice of greed, and you can turn a gift for one into a gift for many."
"The land belongs to nature as far as our eyes can see. The higher we climb, the more we can see."
The goblins laughed as the elf ran away, until more came back.
"Though you may leave this haven we have found, may our strength never leave you."
"She is truly Wirewood's child now." —Elvish refugee
"Instinct is undaunted by terror, unchained by logic. It is the path from which all other paths diverge." —*Volume V, The Book of Life*
Its lock changes to fit each key.
Itself a product of Ixidor's tortured psyche, the chisel brings his darkest dreams to life.
The pattern of life can be studied like a book, if you know how to read it.
